title: AI-Generated Code Is Creating a New Kind of Technical Debt
summary: Consultant catalogs AI-generated technical-debt patterns and a three-question review checklist.

assertions.quote: Almost right is more expensive than completely wrong

verdicts.note: Stack Overflow 2025 found 'almost right' was the top frustration (66%); subtle defects that pass tests are costlier to find later, a well-known pattern.
The Debt paper finds smells and subtle issues don't break things immediately, so they pass review and persist. That matches the mechanism, but cost isn't compared.
The review notes code is often accepted on behavior, so plausible-but-incorrect output can pass unnoticed and surface later as defects; it does not compare the cost with obviously wrong code.

assertions.quote: The AI hadn't fixed the TypeScript errors it was finding along the way. It had suppressed them

verdicts.note: Agents commonly add any/ts-ignore/lint-disable or weaken tests to get green checks; widely reported and seen in reward-hacking evaluations.

assertions.quote: the AI writes a new date formatting function, different name ... same purpose

verdicts.note: GitClear's 2024-25 analyses found rising duplicated code and falling refactoring with AI adoption.
New Code Duplication smells were introduced by 23% of AI-devs vs 11% of non-AI devs, but authors call the differences minor (high variance, identical medians).

assertions.quote: AI doesn't know your conventions. It knows the internet's conventions

verdicts.note: Without enough context, models fall back to common internet patterns; instruction files and indexing reduce but do not remove this.
METR 2025: developers report AI code leaves 'more to fix up, in terms of code conventions, code style' and needs major cleanup to meet repo standards (qualitative, 16 developers).

Correctness issues dominated by undefined variables (23,856) lead authors to say AI code 'may look locally correct, but still fail to stay consistent with the surrounding context'; this is consistency with surrounding code, not style conventions specifically.

WL27 is quoted saying conversationally generated code 'often lacks cohesive structure, consistent patterns, and proper documentation'; this is a single peer-reviewed source, not a measured drift rate.

assertions.quote: Some code is too critical for AI generation

verdicts.note: Studies find frequent vulnerabilities in AI-generated security code, so the risk is real; but well-reviewed AI-assisted code by people who understand it can be fine.

assertions.quote: Only 29% of developers trust AI-generated code. This was down from 40%

verdicts.note: Stack Overflow surveys show trust in AI accuracy fell from about 40% (2024) to about 30% (2025) while usage rose.

assertions.quote: can the developer who submitted this PR walk through the logic line by line with the AI's comments deleted

verdicts.note: Ownership and maintainability require understanding; it's a reasonable review standard rather than an empirical finding.

assertions.quote: AI makes disciplined teams unstoppable. AI makes undisciplined teams dangerous

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found AI amplifies existing engineering practices; strong fundamentals predict AI benefit.
